The washer's washing is Sunnah, except that the corpse has become impure, so when it touches the living with its moisture he becomes impure, and this is the meaning of ghusl being obligatory, by appointment (bi-l-nasb)'

quote: the right to lead prayer belongs to seven, ranked one above another in precedence. Our master Jafar ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (ع) said:
english_says: Introduces al-Sadiq's saying, then gives only the Arabic block with no English rendering
arabic: يؤم القوم أقدمهم هجرة فان استووا فأقرأهم ... فأفقههم ... فأكبرهم سناً وصاحب المسجد أحق بمسجده والإمام ومن أقامه أحق من جميعهم والمرأة تصلي بالنساء ولا تتقدمهن - The one earliest in emigration leads; then best reciter; then most learned in fiqh; then oldest; the mosque's owner has more right; the imam and his appointee above all; a woman leads women standing among them, not ahead
suggested: Add English: 'The people are led by the one earliest in emigration; if equal, the best reciter; if equal in memorising the Quran, the most learned in jurisprudence; if equal in knowledge, the eldest. The owner of a mosque has more right to it, and the imam (ع) and whoever he appoints has more right than all of them. A woman prays with the women and does not stand ahead of them; they stand on her right and left.'
note: Dropped translation of the seven-tier ranking and the woman-imam ruling; the Arabic is present but unrendered.

quote: I turn now to zakat الْفِطْر.
english_says: Arabic word inside English
arabic: زكاة الفطر - zakat of the Fitr
suggested: I turn now to the zakat of Fitr.
note: Complete sentence otherwise.

quote: أَنَا أَعْرِفُ مَنَازِلَ السَّمَاءِ أَحْسَنَ مِمَّا تَعْرِفُونَ مَنَازِلَ الْأَرْضِ.
english_says: Gives a second hadith variant (I know the stations of the sky better than you know the stations of the earth) as a separate block.
arabic: The source quotes only one saying here: أنا بطرقات السماء أعرف منكم بطرقات الأرض (I know the roads of the sky better than you know the roads of the earth). No second variant on p.248.
suggested: Delete the second block (or confirm it is sourced elsewhere in the book).
note: Added text not in this chapter's Arabic; harmless in meaning but not in the source.

quote: "Fast at its sighting and break the fast at its sighting."
english_says: Fast at its sighting
arabic: صوموا لرؤيته = fast for/because of its sighting (lam); the whole later argument turns on the lam meaning 'in preparation for', and the chapter itself later renders it 'Fast for its sighting'
suggested: "Fast for its sighting and break the fast for its sighting."
note: Inconsistent rendering; 'at' pre-empts the lam argument.

quote: and from disobedience toward His guardians, may (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), after submission and certainty
english_says: Stray Arabic blessing formula inside a sentence.
arabic: صلوات الله عليه/عليهم = God's blessings upon them
suggested: and from disobedience toward His guardians, blessings of God upon them, after submission and certainty
note: Also: 'and from His guardians upon His earth — (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) — and I have named it' (p.256), same fix.

quote: Then I say to the hostile party and the rest of the opponents
english_says: hostile party
arabic: ثم نقول الناصبة وغيرهم من المخالفين = the Nasibis (those who show enmity to the Imams' family) and other dissenters
suggested: Then I say to the Nasibis and the rest of the opponents
note: Named group flattened to a generic; low impact.

quote: faulting them in community matters and reproaching them for beginning the fast before the general public
english_says: faulting them in community matters
arabic: طعناً عنهم عن الجماعة (OCR-garbled, likely طعناً عليهم في مفارقة الجماعة) = attacking them for separating from the community
suggested: faulting them for departing from the community
note: OCR uncertain.

quote: Nothing I have set down was mine to originate; it was only an ordering of what has been received. The fitting seal upon such a work is thanks, not claim.
english_says: Author disclaims originating anything; the work is only an ordering of what was received.
arabic: Source has only: 'and after, I have sealed the treatise with praise of Allah...' (وبعد فقد ختمت الرسالة بالحمد لله...). No such disclaimer.
suggested: Delete the two added sentences.
note: Added claim not in source (translator expansion).

quote: That likeness is not an ornament. Just as the moon in the night sky carries a light it has received and gives it to those who travel while others sleep, so the pure Imams stand in the darkness of the age, luminous by what has been entrusted to them and not by what they claim for themselves. The same order continues unbroken in the Imam of our own time.
english_says: Extended commentary on the moons-in-darkness image and continuity to the present Imam.
arabic: Source only has 'أقمار الدجى' then continues 'وإمام الزمان مولانا...'. No commentary.
suggested: Delete the added paragraph.
note: Added text not in source.

quote: This is the order I have been tracing throughout: knowledge descends, obedience ascends, and the two meet in the one whom Allah has appointed.
english_says: Added summary paragraph about order, light not of one's own making, request for steadfastness.
arabic: Source goes directly from 'أفضل التحيات والتسليم' to 'ونسأل الله أن يثبتنا...'. No such paragraph.
suggested: Delete the added paragraph.
note: Added text not in source.

quote: مَا تَمَّ شَعْبَانُ وَلَا نَقَصَ رَمَضَانُ
english_says: No English rendering of the block; prose says only 'thirty days without deficiency, by the word of our masters'.
arabic: ما تم شعبان ولا نقص رمضان = Sha'ban is not complete and Ramadan is not deficient
suggested: Add: "Shaban is never complete, and Ramadan is never deficient."
note: Saying is the proof-text; the prose depends on it.

quote: وَالشَّمْسِ وَضُحَاهَا وَالْقَمَرِ إِذَا تَلَاهَا
english_says: Verse block with no English.
arabic: Q 91:1-2: By the sun and its brightness, and the moon when it follows it
suggested: Add translation: "By the sun and its brightness, and the moon when it follows it."
note: Prose does not depend on it, but every other verse in the list is translated.

quote: the Imam who rules by the command of Allah, the Commander of the Faithful
english_says: Descriptive phrase.
arabic: الإمام الحاكم بأمر الله أمير المؤمنين = the Imam al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah (proper name/title), Commander of the Faithful
suggested: the Imam al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah, Commander of the Faithful
note: Proper title/name rendered as a description; could be read as a generic epithet. Faithful in sense but loses the name.

quote: whoever does anything of that fighting without his command and sheds blood without his permission is held answerable for it
english_says: held answerable
arabic: فهو مقود به = he is subject to retaliation (qawad) for it
suggested: is liable to retaliation for it
note: Weakened legal force; doubtful, OCR reading plausible.

quote: for the moon stood from the sun at the end of the month at a like number of degrees
english_says: at the end of the month
arabic: في آخره = at the end of it (that day)
suggested: at the end of that day at a like number of degrees
note: Referent is that 29th day, not the month; also the causal link (كان) in OCR is unclear.
